correctness_confidence.basis: The single-instrument regression and its degrees of freedom agree with the archived call. Numerical reproduction of both tables and five row-level refits per bootstrap design supports the narrow inference statement.

rigor.basis: The outcome, sample and controls stay fixed across comparisons. The district bootstrap allows a distinct dependence pattern. District-level signs do not address common destination shocks across districts.

novelty.basis: A specific discrepancy and its quantified consequences in this replication deposit are the contribution. The tests and resampling methods have established antecedents; priority over other audits is unverified.

significance.basis: The inference readers can associate with one historical literacy column changes at a conventional threshold. The paper makes no attempt to resolve the wider causal question.

reproducibility.basis: Two clean builds yielded the same PDF and both numerical scripts reproduced their pinned results. For reuse of the PDF alone, the reproduction paragraph would benefit from a direct link to the analysis commit and explicit software versions.

summary: This two-page replication audit ties a diagnostic mismatch to an actual inferential consequence. For 47 judicial districts, demand alone gives a bootstrap p-value of 0.1246 and adding the historical interaction gives 0.0282. I inspected both rendered pages and participated in the audit, drafting and verification in this same context. The finding supports a correction to how the archived column is read; it cannot establish which instruments are valid.
strengths: Tracks specific estimation and reporting calls and matches the printed point estimate.
Distinguishes the overidentification test from testing zero effect and reports Monte Carlo uncertainty separately.
Compares geographic dependence assumptions on a common sample and supplies deletion diagnostics.
weaknesses: The publisher's typeset table could not be inspected; comparison is limited to the archive and working paper.
The standalone PDF lacks a direct pinned link to the scripts and a citation for the wild bootstrap procedure.
The conventional dichotomy at 5% is easier to interpret alongside an inverted confidence set, which is not supplied.
potential_errors: Treating the two different p-values as a test that the coefficients differ would be an incorrect inference. The text reports decisions within each specification.
Assuming judicial districts exhaust relevant economic dependence could understate uncertainty in both tests.
strong_novelty_candidates: Case-specific demonstration that aligning the diagnostic and the archived coefficient changes the zero-effect inference at two levels of geographic clustering.
